title: Optional

members.name: is
members.summary:
Answers whether the Optional is the given one, or whether it holds the given bare value.

Two Optionals are equal when they are the same Case and hold equal values. An empty Optional is never equal to a bare value. An Optional holding an Optional reaches the first entry, so `#Value(#Empty)::is(#Empty)` asks about the receiver and answers `false`. The Method is available whenever the payload conforms to `Equatable`.

entries.signature: is<ItemType is Equatable>(_ other: Optional<ItemType>) -> Boolean
entries.returns: `true` when both are empty, or both hold equal values.

entries.signature: is<ItemType is Equatable>(_ other: ItemType) -> Boolean

parameters.description: the bare value to compare against

entries.returns: `true` when the Optional holds a value equal to it; `false` when it is empty.

members.name: isNot
members.summary:
Answers whether the Optional differs from the given one, or whether it does not hold the given bare value.

An empty Optional holds no bare value, so it always differs from one. The Method is available whenever the payload conforms to `Equatable`.

entries.signature: isNot<ItemType is Equatable>(_ other: Optional<ItemType>) -> Boolean
entries.returns: `true` when the two differ in Case or in value.

entries.signature: isNot<ItemType is Equatable>(_ other: ItemType) -> Boolean

parameters.description: the bare value to compare against

entries.returns: `true` when the Optional is empty or holds a different value.

entries.summary:
Answers the Optional as a String, written `Value(…)` or `Empty`.

The payload renders through its own `toString`, and a String payload is quoted: `#Value("a")` answers `Value("a")`. A String prints bare on its own and quoted inside a structure. The Method is available whenever the payload conforms to `Printable`.
entries.returns: the text `Value(…)` around the payload, or `Empty`.

members.name: hasValue
members.summary: Answers whether the Optional holds a value, or holds a value the check accepts.
members.returns: `true` when there is a value, or when the check accepts the value.

entries.summary: Answers whether the Optional holds a value.

Answers whether the Optional holds a value the check accepts.

An empty Optional answers `false`, and the check does not run.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: the question asked of the value

entries.returns: `true` when there is a value and the check accepts it.

entries.summary: Answers whether the Optional holds no value, the opposite of `hasValue`.

Answers the value, or the given fallback when there is none.

The call collapses an Optional back to a bare value: `list::firstItem()::value(defaultingTo 0)`.

parameters.name: defaultingTo
parameters.description: the value to answer with when there is none

entries.returns: the value, or the fallback in its place.

entries.summary:
Answers the value transformed, wrapped in an Optional.

An empty Optional answers empty, and the transform does not run. This is `List::map` for the at-most-one case.

parameters.description: the transform to run on the value

entries.returns: the transformed value in an Optional, or an empty Optional.

entries.summary:
Answers with the Optional the step answers for the value.

The two Optionals do not nest: the answer has one level. An empty Optional answers empty, and the step does not run.

parameters.description: the step to run on the value

entries.returns: the Optional the step answers, or an empty Optional.

entries.summary:
Answers the Optional when its value passes the check, and empty otherwise.

An empty Optional answers empty, and the check does not run. This is `List::everyItem(where:)` for the at-most-one case.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: the question asked of the value

entries.returns: the Optional unchanged when the value passes, an empty Optional otherwise.

entries.summary:
Answers the Optional when it holds a value, and the given Optional otherwise.

A chain of calls reads as a list of fallbacks, and the first value in it decides the answer. Two empty Optionals answer empty. The Argument is read whether or not the receiver holds a value.

parameters.description: the Optional to fall back on

entries.returns: the receiver when it holds a value, and the Argument in its place otherwise.

entries.summary:
Answers the two values in one Record, and empty when either Optional is empty.

This is `List::pair(with:)` for the at-most-one case. Both values are needed, so one empty Optional answers empty.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: the Optional to pair the value with

entries.returns: a Record holding this value under `first` and the other under `second`, or an empty Optional.

entries.summary:
Answers a List holding the value, and the empty List when there is none.

The answer holds one item at most. It is the bridge to the Methods a List answers, and `OptionalList::values()` is the bridge back.
entries.returns: the List of the value, or the empty List.

entries.summary:
Answers the value as a Result, failing with the given reason where there is none.

An Optional says that there is no value, and a Result says why. The reason is read whether or not it is used.

The reason's own Type decides the Result's failure Type. A bare `#NotFound` binds it to that Case alone, and a `Problem#NotFound` written out does the same. The next call in the chain then works on a Result of a Type it does not expect. Bind the reason to a Constant annotated with the Choice to say the Choice.

parameters.name: failingWith
parameters.description: the reason to fail with where there is no value

entries.returns: the value in a Result, or the reason as a failure.

entries.summary:
Answers the inner Optional, one level down.

An empty outer Optional answers empty.
